competency.title: Isolate, gauge and prove an elevator or escalator machine before returning it to service

completionRule: every station has a passing attempt (stars >= 2, no unsafe action)

ladder.note: a lesson is one station step under one condition; see docs/ladders.md

name: Elevator Constructor — IUEC Core Skills

stations.why: Setting the first guide rail in a new hoistway from a false car, with the platform's own stop switch confirmed and a tag line never out of a hand while the hoist is running.
Proving the traction machine's brake against its own wear limits, with the hand-release lever physically guarded so nobody can pull it while the reading is being taken.
A full pit service — refuge space, ladder, sump pump, and both the spring and oil buffers proven against their own ratings before anyone climbs back out.
Riding the car top itself on inspection operation, watching crosshead clearance, the traveling cable and the door hangers from the one vantage point that actually shows them.
Gauging a car door's interlock gap and closing force, then proving the reopening device actually stops the door on an obstruction rather than assuming it would.
Isolating an escalator to gauge its step chain tension and skirt clearance, then proving the comb, skirt and handrail safety switches with an actual test, not a look.
Walking a hoist rope set by gloved hand for broken wire and dry sections, then gauging tension, diameter and the sheave groove against the limits each one is retired at.
A coordinated rescue with a responding fire company — the car's true position confirmed before a hand crank ever lowers it, and the sill bridged before a passenger ever steps toward the gap.

summary: Eight jobs across new installation, machine room, pit, car top, door, escalator, rope and a coordinated rescue — the isolation habit proven fresh each time against a different machine and a different way of getting hurt.
union: IUEC and the NEIEP apprenticeship as a body
